description: Ordination hall of a wat, a rectangular pillared hall under steep multi-tiered roofs with horned gable finials and boundary stones at its corners.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Rectangular temple ordination hall under steeply pitched overlapping tiled roofs in three descending tiers, curved horn-shaped finials at each gable ridge end, carved triangular gable panel above the entrance, a colonnade of thick square columns around the outside supporting deep eaves, wide stepped entrance platform, small pointed boundary marker stones set at the corners Materials: Orange and green glazed roof tiles, gilded and mirror-inlaid gable carving dulled with dust, whitewashed stucco walls with damp staining at the base, red-lacquered columns worn at hand height, weathered grey boundary stones.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87 -- up from 0.83, and the silhouette layer from 0.80 to 0.90 on the re-declared envelope: band table mean |delta width| 0.017 and |delta depth| 0.044 against 0.173 / 0.446. 3,992/32,000 triangles, 15/24 draw calls, 7/16 materials, 15/32 unique geometries, 4 canvas textures at 5.3 MB, factory 68 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 13.90 x 16.92 x 24.00 m against a declared 14 x 17 x 24, the long axis on Z; band table against the Meshy proxy mean |delta width| 0.017, |delta depth| 0.044 of height (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs).
featureReviews.notes: The first build was declared 12 m tall on a 24 m hall and read as a lid on a box; the proxy of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.709 : 0.573 and the registry was re-declared to 14 x 17 x 24 for this rebuild. Every register height is read off the proxy's orthographic elevations (front.mjs side and end, occupancy map): skirt eaves hw 6.8 at 6.9 m, middle eaves hw 5.0 at 9.0 m, top eaves hw 3.1 at 10.9 m, ridges 14.8 m and 14.0 m, apex chofa to 17.0 m. The one band still over 0.05 is band 4 (6.8-8.5 m): the proxy's skirt fascia is taller than the 0.4 m built. Raising the skirt by 0.5 m halved that residual; the rest is the fascia's own height and is reported rather than chased.

featureReviews.evidence: A hipped 37-degree portico skirt, a 45-degree middle layer the full 18 m, and a top gable telescoped into a 12 m centre at 14.8 m and two 3 m ends at 14.0 m, each register a white riser, a glaze band and a tile field; white bargeboards with red strips; sixteen curved horns; one carved pediment per end gable.
featureReviews.notes: The first build nested three same-length tiers concentrically -- a wedding cake, not a Thai roof -- which is the structure the user returned. The proxy's side elevation shows the layer lines continuous along the length with only the ridges stepping, and its end elevation shows one gable triangle from the middle eaves to the ridge, so the end sections' top pitch is the middle layer's 45 degrees continued and the top layer's step shows only on the side slopes. The centre section's gable faces at z = +-6 show 0.8 m above the end ridges, which is the telescoped step the plate shows behind the near pediment. The skirt is quad-strip rings because it hips round the ends and no extrusion can do that; it closes with a soffit and an inner wall so the turntable gate cannot read through it.

featureReviews.evidence: Thirty red columns in a regular peristyle at ONE draw call under a red eaves beam, a parapet between their bases, sixteen windows and two doors in stone surrounds on the body, and eight bai sema on the bottom terrace with one centred before each stair.
featureReviews.notes: Counted off the plate's right-hand elevation: eleven a side and four between the corners on each end, against the first build's nine and three. The body was bare in the first build; the plate shows dark leaves in white surrounds between every column, and they are two instanced systems rather than thirty-two meshes. The sema are required by the registry notes -- they are what make this an ORDINATION hall -- so they are an asset feature and not dressing.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.735-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate, and four seamless Canvas 2D weathering tiles bound post-construction: streaked whitewash, peeling lacquer, laid tile courses with moss, and a carved gilt pediment. 4 textures, 5.3 MB, 68 ms.
featureReviews.notes: The user's brief was 'add a weathered texture on the outside' and the plate agrees: the whitewash is streaked grey-black and grimed at the plinth (600..700, 850..878 measures #828282 against the clean #BDA69A), the columns peel to pale plaster (p90 #C8A58C), the roof is laid in visible courses with grey-green growth. Each tile is a multiplier of measured ratios on the measured albedo, bound as map AND bumpMap; the lacquer is re-based to the plaster envelope so its flakes can be brighter than the red. The first pass at sixteen flakes per tile read as spots, not peel, and was cut to six; the first stone pass read as a barcode of streaks and was softened to blurred washes. Dark cores are held at 0.62 of clean for the luma-58 hole gate.

name: Ubosot
notes: The most sacred building of a wat and its visual anchor. Its identity is the roof: a wrap-around portico skirt, then a layered gable roof telescoped into three sections along the length -- the centre ridge higher than the two ends -- every slope broken into stepped layers with glazed eaves bands, white bargeboards and curved chofa horns at every apex and rake foot. The small pointed boundary marker stones at the corners are what make it an ordination hall specifically rather than a general assembly hall, so they belong to this asset and are not optional dressing. Declared 14 x 17 x 24 m: the 24 m length is correct for a full ordination hall, and the height and width were re-declared on 2026-08-26 from the Meshy proxy of the plate (long:h:short = 1 : 0.71 : 0.57), after the first build at 12 m tall read as squat against the reference. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
